title: Notre année scientifique en révision
oneGoal: Students will identify and recall the main science topics they explored during the year
decisionPoints: What science topics were most memorable for students this year?
Should we use a timeline format or topic-by-topic review?
Are students ready to make connections between different science units?
progression: Foundation lesson - activates prior knowledge and sets the stage for showcasing learning
realWorldConnection: Reflecting on learning helps us understand how much we've grown, like looking at photos from the beginning of the year

title: Nos découvertes les plus excitantes
oneGoal: Students will identify their most exciting scientific discoveries from the year and explain why they were special
decisionPoints: Should students share discoveries individually or in small groups?
How can we help students who struggle to identify favorite discoveries?
Are students ready to explain their thinking or should we focus on sharing experiences?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by helping students identify personally meaningful science learning moments
realWorldConnection: Scientists often share their most exciting discoveries with others, just like we share exciting news with friends

title: Qu'est-ce qu'une exposition scientifique?
oneGoal: Students will understand what a science fair or exposition is and how scientists share their work
decisionPoints: Should we show examples of science fairs or focus on simple sharing concepts?
How can we make the concept accessible without overwhelming students?
Are students ready to understand audience or should we focus on showing work?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by introducing the concept of formal science sharing and celebration
realWorldConnection: Understanding how people share their best work at art shows, school concerts, or sports games

title: Choisir notre projet de démonstration
oneGoal: Students will select one science topic or experiment from the year to demonstrate at the exposition
decisionPoints: Should students choose individually or work in small groups?
What criteria should guide project selection (interest, success, safety)?
Are students ready for independent choice or need guided options?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by helping students select specific content for their exposition participation
realWorldConnection: Making choices about what to share, like picking our best artwork for a family display

title: Planifier notre démonstration
oneGoal: Students will create a simple plan for how they will show their chosen science topic to visitors
decisionPoints: Should we provide planning templates or encourage creative formats?
How detailed should the planning be for Grade 1 students?
Are students ready for thinking about audience needs or focus on their own presentation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by developing organizational skills for science communication
realWorldConnection: Planning how to explain something to others, like teaching a game to a younger child

title: Matériel et outils nécessaires
oneGoal: Students will identify and gather the materials they need for their science demonstration
decisionPoints: Which materials are safe and appropriate for student-led demonstrations?
Should we focus on simple materials or allow more complex tools with supervision?
Are students ready for material responsibility or need teacher-prepared sets?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by developing practical preparation skills and safety awareness
realWorldConnection: Getting ready for activities by gathering what we need, like packing for a trip or preparing for cooking

title: Pratiquer notre explication simple
oneGoal: Students will practice explaining their science topic using simple words that other children can understand
decisionPoints: Should students practice with peers or adults first?
How can we help students use age-appropriate vocabulary?
Are students ready for feedback on their explanations or need encouragement first?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by developing oral communication skills for science content
realWorldConnection: Learning to explain things clearly so others understand, like telling someone how to play our favorite game

title: Créer un affichage visuel
oneGoal: Students will create a simple visual display (drawing, poster, or model) to support their science demonstration
decisionPoints: What visual formats are most appropriate for Grade 1 science concepts?
Should we focus on drawings, simple posters, or 3D models?
Are students ready for independent creation or need guided templates?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by adding visual communication skills to support oral explanations
realWorldConnection: Using pictures and displays to help explain ideas, like showing photos when telling about vacation

title: Questions que les visiteurs pourraient poser
oneGoal: Students will anticipate and practice answering simple questions about their science topic
decisionPoints: What types of questions are most likely from different age groups?
Should we practice specific questions or general question-answering skills?
Are students ready for unknown questions or should we stick to predictable ones?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by preparing students for interactive science communication
realWorldConnection: Being ready to answer questions about things we know well, like explaining our favorite books or toys

title: Sécurité pendant notre démonstration
oneGoal: Students will identify and practice safety rules for their science demonstration with visitors
decisionPoints: Which safety considerations are most important for student-led demonstrations?
Should we focus on material safety or visitor safety protocols?
Are students ready for safety leadership or need adult supervision reminders?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by reinforcing safety awareness in public science sharing contexts
realWorldConnection: Being responsible for safety when showing others our activities, like teaching someone to ride a bike safely

title: Première pratique complète
oneGoal: Students will perform a complete run-through of their science demonstration with classmates as audience
decisionPoints: Should students present individually or in small groups?
How can we provide supportive feedback without discouraging students?
Are students ready for peer feedback or should we focus on teacher observation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by providing practical experience with their complete demonstration
realWorldConnection: Practicing performances before the real event, like rehearsing for a school play or music concert

title: Améliorer notre présentation
oneGoal: Students will identify one specific improvement they can make to their science demonstration
decisionPoints: Should improvements focus on content clarity or presentation skills?
How can we help students identify achievable improvements?
Are students ready for self-reflection or need guided improvement suggestions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by developing reflective improvement skills and growth mindset
realWorldConnection: Making things better through practice and changes, like improving at sports or drawing

title: Aider les autres avec leurs projets
oneGoal: Students will provide helpful feedback and encouragement to classmates preparing their demonstrations
decisionPoints: What feedback skills are appropriate for Grade 1 students to practice?
Should we focus on positive comments or specific suggestions?
Are students ready for peer evaluation or should we model supportive language?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by developing collaborative skills and scientific community values
realWorldConnection: Helping friends get better at things they're working on, like cheering each other on during games

title: Inviter notre famille
oneGoal: Students will create invitations for their families to attend the science exposition
decisionPoints: Should invitations include specific details about student demonstrations?
How can we make invitations accessible for all family situations?
Are students ready for writing invitations or should we use templates/dictation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by connecting school science learning with family engagement
realWorldConnection: Inviting people we care about to see our special work, like asking grandparents to come to graduation

title: Préparer notre espace d'exposition
oneGoal: Students will organize their demonstration space and materials for the science exposition
decisionPoints: How much space and setup responsibility can Grade 1 students handle?
Should we focus on individual spaces or collaborative classroom setup?
Are students ready for independent organization or need step-by-step guidance?
progression: Builds on Lesson 14 by developing organizational skills and event preparation
realWorldConnection: Getting ready for special events by organizing our space, like setting up for a birthday party

title: Répétition générale
oneGoal: Students will perform a final practice run of their science demonstration with timing and setup
decisionPoints: Should the dress rehearsal include other classes as audience?
How can we address last-minute concerns without creating anxiety?
Are students ready for independent performance or need support reminders?
progression: Builds on Lesson 15 by providing confidence-building final preparation before the exposition
realWorldConnection: Final practice before important events to make sure everything goes smoothly, like rehearsing before performing

title: Notre exposition scientifique!
oneGoal: Students will successfully demonstrate their science learning to visitors at the exposition event
decisionPoints: How can we support nervous students during the actual event?
Should students rotate as both presenters and audience members?
How do we ensure every student feels successful regardless of performance?
progression: Builds on Lesson 16 by implementing all preparation in the actual exposition event
realWorldConnection: Sharing our learning and hard work with others in a special celebration of what we've accomplished

title: Célébrer nos réussites
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their successful participation in the science exposition and celebrate their growth
decisionPoints: Should celebration focus on individual achievements or collective success?
How can we help students identify specific growth and learning?
Are students ready for formal reflection or should we use informal sharing?
progression: Builds on Lesson 17 by helping students recognize and celebrate their scientific and presentation growth
realWorldConnection: Feeling proud of accomplishments and recognizing how much we've learned and grown

title: Apprendre des autres projets
oneGoal: Students will identify interesting ideas and discoveries they learned from other students' demonstrations
decisionPoints: Should we structure learning observations or allow free exploration?
How can we help students articulate what they found interesting?
Are students ready for comparing approaches or should we focus on appreciation?
progression: Builds on Lesson 18 by extending learning through peer observation and scientific community appreciation
realWorldConnection: Learning new things from friends and family, discovering that everyone has interesting knowledge to share

title: Sciences pour l'été
oneGoal: Students will identify safe science exploration opportunities they can pursue during summer break
decisionPoints: Which summer science activities are safest and most accessible for families?
Should we focus on observation activities or simple experiments?
Are students ready for independent science thinking or need structured suggestions?
progression: Culminating lesson - extends science learning beyond school year and maintains scientific curiosity during break
realWorldConnection: Continuing to explore and discover during summer through nature walks, backyard observations, and safe family experiments
